words.tr: n. 状态；条件；环境；
words.ex: His condition improved after the treatment.
words.ex_cn: 他的状况在接受治疗后好转了。
words.en: A condition is a state of affairs that must exist or be brought about before something else can happen or be done.

words.tr: n. 疾病；
words.ex: The doctor treated his disease with medicine.
words.ex_cn: 医生用药物治疗了他的疾病。
words.en: A disease is an illness that affects people, animals, or plants, often caused by infection or a failure of health rather than by an accident.

words.tr: adj. 敏锐的；急性的；严重的；
words.ex: He has an acute mind and solves problems quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他思维敏锐，能快速解决问题。
words.en: An acute problem or negative feeling is very severe.

words.tr: adj. 长期的；慢性的；
words.ex: He has a chronic cough that lasts for months.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个持续数月的慢性咳嗽。
words.en: A chronic illness or condition lasts for a long time and cannot be cured, but it can usually be controlled.

words.tr: adj. 传染性的；有感染力的；
words.ex: The virus is infectious and spreads quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒具有传染性，传播迅速。
words.en: An infectious disease can be passed from one person to another, especially through the air they breathe.

words.tr: phrase. 遗传病；先天性疾病
words.ex: Huntington's disease is an inherited disease that affects the brain.
words.ex_cn: 亨廷顿氏病是一种影响大脑的遗传病。
words.en: A disease or disorder that is inherited genetically.

words.tr: 我有
words.ex: I have a book about algebra.
words.ex_cn: 我有一本关于代数的书。
words.en: Used to state possession or experience of something.

words.tr: 我患有；我受...之苦
words.ex: I suffer from headaches every day.
words.ex_cn: 我每天都头痛。
words.en: Used to indicate enduring a medical condition or problem.

words.tr: phrase. 我一直遭受……之苦；我长期患有（某种疾病或痛苦）
words.ex: I have been suffering from a cold for three days.
words.ex_cn: 我感冒已经三天了。
words.en: Used to describe a medical condition that has persisted over time.

words.tr: 短语. 我被诊断出患有
words.ex: I have been diagnosed with diabetes.
words.ex_cn: 我被诊断出患有糖尿病。
words.en: Used to state that a medical professional has identified a specific illness.

words.tr: n. 高血压；过度紧张
words.ex: He has hypertension and takes medicine every day.
words.ex_cn: 他有高血压，每天吃药。
words.en: Hypertension is a condition in which the force of the blood against the artery walls is too high.

words.tr: phrase. 心脏病
words.ex: He has heart disease and must eat healthy food.
words.ex_cn: 他患有心脏病，必须吃健康的食物。
words.en: A condition that affects the heart and blood vessels, often leading to serious health issues.

words.tr: n. 糖尿病；
words.ex: He has diabetes and must check his blood every day.
words.ex_cn: 他患有糖尿病，必须每天检查血糖。
words.en: A medical condition in which the body cannot produce enough insulin or cannot use insulin properly, leading to high levels of sugar in the blood.

words.tr: n. 结核病；肺结核；
words.ex: He was diagnosed with tuberculosis last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年被诊断出患有结核病。
words.en: Tuberculosis is an infectious disease caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis, which primarily affects the lungs but can also affect other parts of the body.

words.tr:
adj. 寒冷的；冰冷的；
n. 寒冷；
words.ex: The cold wind made me shiver.
words.ex_cn: 寒冷的风让我发抖。
words.en: Something that is cold has a low temperature, especially when compared to the temperature of the human body. It can also describe a lack of warmth in someone's behavior or a situation.

words.tr: phrase. 感冒；亏本
words.ex: He goes out without a coat and catches a cold.
words.ex_cn: 他出去时没穿外套，结果感冒了。
words.en: To become ill with a cold.

words.tr: n. 发烧
words.ex: He has a high fever and stays in bed.
words.ex_cn: 他发烧了，躺在床上休息。
words.en: A fever is a condition in which the body's temperature is higher than usual, often as a response to infection.

words.tr: n. 过敏症；
words.ex: He has an allergy to peanuts.
words.ex_cn: 他对花生过敏。
words.en: An allergy is a condition in which your immune system reacts abnormally to a foreign substance.

words.tr: phrase. 对…过敏
words.ex_cn: 他对花生过敏。
words.en: If you are allergic to something, you become ill or get a rash when you eat it, smell it, or touch it.

words.tr: phrase. 枯草热；花粉病
words.ex: He has hay fever in spring.
words.ex_cn: 他在春天患花粉热。
words.en: A common allergic condition affecting the mucous membranes of the nose, eyes, and air passages, typically caused by an allergy to pollen or dust.

words.tr: n. 癌；癌症；
words.ex: He was diagnosed with cancer last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年被诊断出患有癌症。
words.en: Cancer is a serious disease caused by cells that are not normal and that can spread to other parts of the body.

words.tr: n. 哮喘
words.ex: He has asthma and cannot run fast.
words.ex_cn: 他有哮喘，不能跑快。
words.en: A respiratory condition marked by spasms in the bronchi of the lungs, causing difficulty in breathing. It usually results from an allergic reaction or other forms of hypersensitivity.

words.tr: n. 肺炎
words.ex: He got pneumonia after a bad cold.
words.ex_cn: 他得了重感冒后患了肺炎。
words.en: Pneumonia is a serious disease which affects your lungs and makes it difficult for you to breathe.

words.tr: n. 肝炎
words.ex: He has hepatitis and needs to rest.
words.ex_cn: 他患有肝炎，需要休息。
words.en: Hepatitis is an inflammation of the liver, often caused by a viral infection.

words.tr: n. 肾炎
words.ex: He has nephritis and must drink more water.
words.ex_cn: 他患有肾炎，必须多喝水。
words.en: Nephritis is a condition in which the kidneys become inflamed, leading to impaired kidney function.

words.tr: n. 抑郁；萧条；
words.ex: He felt deep depression after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到深深的抑郁。
words.en: A period during which business, employment, and stock-market values decline severely or remain at a very low level of activity.

words.tr: phrase. 心理问题；精神健康问题
words.ex: He has mental issues and needs help.
words.ex_cn: 他有心理问题，需要帮助。
words.en: Mental issues refer to problems or disorders related to the mind, affecting emotions, thoughts, and behavior.

words.tr: phrase. 食物中毒
words.ex: He got food poisoning from eating bad sushi.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了变质的寿司后食物中毒了。
words.en: Illness caused by consuming contaminated food, characterized by nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal pain.

words.tr: n. 肥胖；肥胖症；
words.ex: Obesity is a serious health problem in many countries.
words.ex_cn: 肥胖是许多国家的一个严重健康问题。
words.en: Obesity is a medical condition in which excess body fat has accumulated to the extent that it may have a negative effect on health.

words.tr: n. 关节炎
words.ex: He has arthritis in his hands.
words.ex_cn: 他双手有关节炎。
words.en: Arthritis is a medical condition in which the joints in someone's body are swollen and painful.

words.tr: n.症状
words.ex: He has symptoms of a cold.
words.ex_cn: 他有感冒的症状。
words.en: A symptom is a physical or mental feature which is regarded as indicating a condition of disease, particularly such a feature that is apparent to the patient.

words.tr: phrase. 我经历；我体验
words.ex: I experience joy when I help others.
words.ex_cn: 当我帮助别人时，我感到快乐。
words.en: Used to describe undergoing or feeling a particular sensation or event.

words.tr: n. 恶心；反胃；作呕；
words.ex: The smell of the food made her feel nausea.
words.ex_cn: 食物的气味让她感到恶心。
words.en: A feeling of sickness with an inclination to vomit.

words.tr: n. 便秘
words.ex: He has constipation after eating too much meat.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多肉后便秘了。
words.en: A condition in which there is difficulty in emptying the bowels, usually associated with hardened feces.

words.tr: n. 疲乏；劳累；
words.ex: After running for an hour, he felt fatigue.
words.ex_cn: 跑了一个小时后，他感到疲乏。
words.en: A feeling of extreme physical or mental tiredness.

words.tr: n. 枯竭；耗尽；筋疲力尽；
words.ex: The long hike led to his exhaustion.
words.ex_cn: 长时间的徒步旅行导致他筋疲力尽。
words.en: A state of extreme physical or mental tiredness.

words.tr:
n. 喷嚏；喷嚏声
v. 打喷嚏
words.ex: He had a cold and let out a loud sneeze.
words.ex_cn: 他感冒了，打了一个响亮的喷嚏。
words.en: To sneeze is to suddenly expel air from the nose and mouth due to irritation in the nasal passages.

words.tr: v. 打喷嚏；“sneeze”的现在分词
words.ex: He is sneezing because of the dust.
words.ex_cn: 他因为灰尘在打喷嚏。
words.en: Sneezing is an involuntary expulsion of air from the nose and mouth caused by irritation of the nostrils.

words.tr:
n. 咳嗽；
v. 咳嗽；
words.ex: He had a bad cough last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚咳得很厉害。
words.en: A cough is a sudden, forceful expulsion of air from the lungs, often caused by irritation in the airway.

words.tr: v. 咳嗽；“cough”的现在分词；
words.ex: He is coughing because he has a cold.
words.ex_cn: 他因为感冒在咳嗽。
words.en: The act of expelling air from the lungs suddenly and noisily, often to keep the respiratory passages free of irritating material.

words.tr: n. 发炎；炎症；燃烧；激动
words.ex: The redness and swelling show inflammation.
words.ex_cn: 发红和肿胀表明有炎症。
words.en: Inflammation is a condition in which a part of your body becomes red, swollen, and painful as a reaction to infection or injury.

words.tr:
v. 呕吐；吐出；喷涌出
n. 呕吐；呕吐物
words.ex: He felt sick and vomited on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 他感到恶心，就在地上吐了。
words.en: To eject matter from the stomach through the mouth.

words.tr: v. 呕吐（vomit 的 ing 形式）
words.ex: He was hospitalized due to severe vomiting.
words.ex_cn: 他因严重呕吐而住院。
words.en: The act of ejecting matter from the stomach through the mouth.

words.tr: phrase. 夜间盗汗；睡觉时大量出汗的现象
words.ex: She suffered from severe night sweats during her illness.
words.ex_cn: 她在生病期间遭受了严重的盗汗。
words.en: Night sweats refer to excessive sweating during the night that is not related to an overheated sleeping environment.

words.tr: phrase. 我的粪便中有血
words.ex: I noticed blood in my stools and decided to see a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 我注意到便血，决定去看医生。
words.en: The presence of blood in the feces, which can be a symptom of various medical conditions.

words.tr:
adj. 麻木的；失去知觉的
v. 使麻木；使迟钝
words.ex: His fingers felt numb after being in the cold.
words.ex_cn: 他的手指在寒冷中变得麻木。
words.en: If a part of your body is numb, you cannot feel it, usually for a short time.

words.tr: n. 麻痹；麻木
words.ex: The cold caused a numbness in my fingers.
words.ex_cn: 寒冷导致我的手指麻木。
words.en: Numbness is a lack of feeling in part of your body, often caused by cold, injury, or emotion.

words.tr: phrase. 睡眠不足；失眠；睡眠缺失
words.ex: The loss of sleep affected his performance at work.
words.ex_cn: n. 失眠影响了他的工作表现。
words.en: The condition of not getting enough sleep, which can affect physical and mental health.

words.tr: phrase. 带血的痰；痰中带血
words.ex: The patient was admitted to the hospital with blood-stained sputum.
words.ex_cn: 病人因带血的痰被送入医院。
words.en: Sputum that contains blood, often indicating a medical condition.

words.tr: n. 头晕；昏眩；头昏眼花
words.ex: He felt dizziness after standing up quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他站起来后感到头晕。
words.en: A sensation of spinning around and losing one's balance.

words.tr: n. 腹泻
words.ex: He had diarrhea after eating bad food.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了坏食物后得了腹泻。
words.en: A condition in which feces are discharged from the bowels frequently and in a liquid form.

words.tr: phrase. 食欲不振；胃口差
words.ex: She has a poor appetite due to her illness.
words.ex_cn: 她因为生病而食欲不振。
words.en: A poor appetite refers to a reduced desire to eat, often due to illness or stress.

words.tr: phrase. 流鼻涕
words.ex: He has a runny nose because of the cold.
words.ex_cn: 他因为感冒而流鼻涕。
words.en: A runny nose is a condition in which liquid mucus runs out of the nose, often as a symptom of a cold or allergy.

words.tr: phrase. 喉咙痛
words.ex: He has a sore throat from singing too much.
words.ex_cn: 他因为唱太多歌而喉咙痛。
words.en: If you have a sore throat, your throat hurts and it is difficult for you to swallow.

words.tr: n. 感染；
words.ex: The wound caused a serious infection.
words.ex_cn: 伤口引起了严重的感染。
words.en: An infection is a disease caused by microorganisms such as bacteria, viruses, or parasites invading the body.

words.tr: phrase. 口臭；口腔异味
words.ex: He has bad breath after eating garlic.
words.ex_cn: 他吃完大蒜后有口臭。
words.en: Bad breath is an unpleasant odor coming from the mouth. It can be caused by various factors, including poor dental hygiene, certain foods, and health conditions.

words.tr: n. 胃灼热
words.ex: The spicy food caused him severe heartburn.
words.ex_cn: 辛辣的食物让他感到严重的胃灼热。
words.en: A burning sensation in the chest, often caused by stomach acid moving up into the esophagus.

words.tr: v. 膨胀；肿胀；“swell”的现在分词；
words.ex: The wound is swelling after the injury.
words.ex_cn: 受伤后伤口在肿胀。
words.en: An abnormal enlargement of a part of the body, typically as a result of an accumulation of fluid.

words.tr: v. 打呼噜，打鼾( snore的现在分词 )
words.ex: He is snoring loudly while sleeping.
words.ex_cn: 他睡觉时打鼾很大声。
words.en: The noisy breathing sound made during sleep.

words.tr:
n. 日灼；晒伤
v. 晒黑；晒伤
words.ex: He got sunburn after swimming all day.
words.ex_cn: 他整天游泳后得了日灼。
words.en: Sunburn is a condition where the skin becomes red, sore, and sometimes swollen and blistered as a result of overexposure to the ultraviolet rays of the sun.

words.tr: n. 医疗保险制度
words.ex: He uses medicare to pay for his doctor visits.
words.ex_cn: 他使用医疗保险支付看医生的费用。
words.en: A system of health insurance for people over 65 in the US, paid for by a combination of payroll taxes and general federal revenue.

words.tr: phrase. 医疗保险卡；联邦医保卡（澳大利亚或美国等国家政府发放，用于享受公共医疗服务的证件）
words.ex: Don't forget to bring your medicare card to the doctor's appointment.
words.ex_cn: 别忘了带你的医疗保险卡去看医生。
words.en: A medicare card is an official document that provides proof of a person's eligibility for government-funded health care services.

words.tr: phrase. 医疗保健卡；健康保险卡
words.ex: I need to renew my healthcare card before it expires.
words.ex_cn: 我需要在医疗卡过期之前续期。
words.en: A healthcare card is a card issued to individuals that allows them to access medical services, often at a reduced cost or for free, depending on the healthcare system in their country.

words.tr: n. 减价票；特许权；
words.ex: He bought a concession ticket for the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他买了电影的减价票。
words.en: A concession is a point or principle that is granted or acknowledged in the course of an argument or negotiation, often as a compromise or to facilitate agreement.

words.tr: phrase. 批量计费；整批账单
words.ex: He is bulking billing for his gym services.
words.ex_cn: 他正在为健身房服务增加收费。
words.en: A colloquial term for excessive or confusing medical charges.

words.tr: phrase. 批量计费；集体账单（尤指澳大利亚医疗体系中医生向政府直接收费的服务方式）
words.ex: The doctor agreed to bulk bill the consultation.
words.ex_cn: 医生同意通过批量账单方式收取咨询费用。
words.en: A method of payment in healthcare where the doctor directly charges the government or insurance company, and the patient does not have to pay any additional fees.

words.tr: phrase. 自付费用；需个人支付的开支
words.ex: He had to cover the out of pocket expenses for the trip.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不支付旅行的自付费用。
words.en: Out of pocket expenses refer to the costs that an individual pays directly from their own money, often for business or personal purposes, which may be reimbursed later.

words.tr: n. 移交；推举；被介绍者；转诊病人
words.ex: He got a referral from his doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他从医生那里得到了转诊介绍。
words.en: The act of directing someone to a different place or person for information, help, or action, often in a professional context.

words.tr: v. 提到；参考；引用；
words.ex: He didn't refer to the book during the talk.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中没有提到那本书。
words.en: If you refer to a particular subject or person, you talk about them or mention them. If you refer to someone or something as a particular thing, you use a particular word, expression, or name to mention or describe them.

words.tr: phrase. 私人健康保险；由非政府保险公司提供的医疗保障计划
words.ex: Many people choose private health insurance for faster access to medical services.
words.ex_cn: 许多人选择私人医疗保险以更快地获得医疗服务。
words.en: Private health insurance refers to health insurance policies that are purchased by individuals or provided by employers, offering coverage that is not part of a government-provided health care system.

words.tr: phrase. 医院保障；医院保险 coverage 指保险范围内对住院等医疗服务的覆盖
words.ex: Does your insurance plan include hospital cover?
words.ex_cn: 你的保险计划包括医院保险吗？
words.en: Hospital cover refers to insurance that pays for the cost of hospital treatment.

words.tr: n. 皮肤病学家；皮肤科医生
words.ex: He visited a dermatologist for his skin rash.
words.ex_cn: 他因为皮肤疹去看皮肤科医生。
words.en: A dermatologist is a doctor who specializes in the study, diagnosis, and treatment of skin disorders and diseases.

words.tr: n. 妇科学家
words.ex: She visited a gynaecologist for a check-up.
words.ex_cn: 她去看妇科医生做检查。
words.en: A gynaecologist is a doctor who specializes in women's health, particularly their reproductive systems.

words.tr: n. 产科医生
words.ex: The obstetrician helped the baby be born.
words.ex_cn: 产科医生帮助婴儿出生。
words.en: An obstetrician is a doctor who specializes in pregnancy, childbirth, and a woman's reproductive system.

words.tr: n. 眼科医师
words.ex: The ophthalmologist recommended regular eye exams to monitor my vision.
words.ex_cn: 眼科医生建议定期进行眼科检查以监测我的视力。
words.en: An ophthalmologist is a medical doctor specializing in the diagnosis and treatment of eye disorders and diseases.

words.tr: n. 验光师；配镜师
words.ex: The optometrist checked my eyes last week.
words.ex_cn: 验光师上周检查了我的眼睛。
words.en: An optometrist is a person whose job is to examine people's eyes and to recommend and sell glasses.

words.tr: n. 儿科医师
words.ex: The paediatrician checks the child's health every month.
words.ex_cn: 儿科医生每个月检查孩子的健康状况。
words.en: A paediatrician is a doctor who specializes in treating children and their diseases.

words.tr: n. 牙科医生
words.ex: He visits the dentist every six months.
words.ex_cn: 他每六个月去看一次牙医。
words.en: A dentist is a person who is qualified to treat diseases and conditions that affect the teeth and gums, especially the repair and extraction of teeth and the insertion of artificial ones.

words.tr: n. 精神病学家；精神科医生
words.ex: He visits a psychiatrist every week.
words.ex_cn: 他每周去看一次精神科医生。
words.en: A psychiatrist is a medical doctor who specializes in the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of mental illnesses and emotional disorders.

words.tr: n. 心理学家；心理学研究者；
words.ex: The psychologist helped the child feel less afraid.
words.ex_cn: 心理学家帮助孩子感觉不那么害怕。
words.en: A psychologist is a person who studies the human mind and human emotions and behaviour, and who uses this knowledge to help people with mental health problems.

words.tr: abbr. 通用的（general purpose）；普通开业医生（general practiti...
words.ex: This is a gp computer for everyday tasks.
words.ex_cn: 这是一台用于日常任务的通用计算机。
words.en: Abbreviation for General Practitioner, a primary care doctor in the UK and other countries.

words.tr: n. 专家；专科医生；
words.ex: He is a specialist in heart surgery.
words.ex_cn: 他是心脏手术方面的专家。
words.en: A specialist is a person who is highly skilled or knowledgeable in a particular field.

words.tr: n. 医生；内科医生；
words.ex: The physician checked the patient's temperature.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了病人的体温。
words.en: A physician is a medical doctor who is trained in the diagnosis and treatment of diseases and injuries.

words.tr: n. 外科医生
words.ex: The surgeon fixed the broken bone.
words.ex_cn: 外科医生修复了断裂的骨头。
words.en: A surgeon is a medical doctor who performs operations.

words.tr: n. 护士；
words.ex: The nurse gave the patient medicine.
words.ex_cn: 护士给病人服了药。
words.en: A nurse is a person whose job is to care for people who are ill or injured, especially in a hospital.

words.tr: n. 助产士；接生婆
words.ex: The midwife helped the baby come out safely.
words.ex_cn: 助产士帮助婴儿安全出生。
words.en: A midwife is a person, usually a woman, who is trained to help women during childbirth.

words.tr: phrase. 救护车急救员；指在救护车上提供紧急医疗救助的专业人员
words.ex: The ambulance paramedic quickly assessed the patient's condition.
words.ex_cn: 救护车急救员迅速评估了病人的状况。
words.en: A paramedic is a person who is trained to give emergency medical treatment or to assist medical professionals.

words.tr: n. 麻醉师
words.ex: The anesthetist gave the patient medicine before surgery.
words.ex_cn: 麻醉师在手术前给病人用了药。
words.en: An anesthetist is a medical specialist who administers anesthetics.

words.tr: n. 饮食学家；营养学家；
words.ex: The dietician helped me plan healthy meals.
words.ex_cn: 饮食学家帮我规划了健康的饮食。
words.en: A dietician is a professional who is qualified to give advice about diet and nutrition.

words.tr: n. 理疗医师; 理疗学家
words.ex: The physiotherapist helped him walk again.
words.ex_cn: 物理治疗师帮助他重新走路。
words.en: A physiotherapist is a person who treats people using physiotherapy.

words.tr: n. 药剂师
words.ex: The pharmacist gave me medicine for my cough.
words.ex_cn: 药剂师给了我治咳嗽的药。
words.en: A pharmacist is a person who is qualified to prepare and dispense medicinal drugs.

words.tr: phrase. 耳鼻喉科专家（治疗耳、鼻、喉疾病的医生）
words.ex: I need to see an ENT specialist for my ear infection.
words.ex_cn: 我需要去看耳鼻喉科专家治疗我的耳部感染。
words.en: An ENT specialist is a medical doctor who specializes in the diagnosis and treatment of disorders related to the ear, nose, and throat.

words.tr: v. 送医院治疗；使住院
words.ex: The doctor decided to hospitalise the patient for further tests.
words.ex_cn: 医生决定让病人住院进行进一步检查。
words.en: To admit someone to a hospital for treatment.

words.tr:
v. 放电；放出；
n. 排放；
words.ex: The battery will discharge if left unused for a long time.
words.ex_cn: 如果长时间不使用，电池会放电。
words.en: If someone is discharged from a hospital, prison, or the armed forces, they are officially allowed to leave, or told that they must leave. If something is discharged from inside a place, it comes out.

words.tr: phrase. 接收处；入院处（医院中负责办理病人入院手续的部门）
words.ex: The admitting office is located on the first floor of the hospital.
words.ex_cn: n. 入院处位于医院的一楼。
words.en: The office in a hospital or other institution where new patients or clients are processed and registered.

words.tr: n. 允许进入；承认；
words.ex: The ticket is your admission to the concert.
words.ex_cn: 这张票是进入音乐会的许可。
words.en: An admission is a statement in which you admit that something bad, unpleasant, or embarrassing is true, or the act of allowing someone to enter a place or organization.

words.tr: phrase. 门诊部：医院中为未住院的患者提供诊断和治疗服务的部门。
words.ex: He went to the out-patient department for a check-up.
words.ex_cn: 他去门诊部做检查。
words.en: A department in a hospital where patients receive diagnosis or treatment without being admitted to the hospital.

words.tr: phrase. 急诊科；急诊室（医院中处理紧急医疗情况的部门）
words.ex: He went to the emergency department after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他去了急诊科。
words.en: The emergency department is a medical treatment facility specializing in emergency medicine, the acute care of patients who present without prior appointment; either by their own means or by that of an ambulance.

words.tr: phrase. 重症监护室；重症监护病房
words.ex: The patient was transferred to the intensive care unit.
words.ex_cn: 病人被转移到加护病房。
words.en: A hospital facility that provides intensive care medicine, which is a special department where patients who are critically ill are treated and monitored closely by healthcare professionals.

words.tr: abbr. 重症监护病房；“Intensive Care Unit”的缩写
words.ex: The patient was transferred to the ICU after surgery.
words.ex_cn: 病人在手术后被转移到重症监护室。
words.en: Intensive Care Unit, a special department of a hospital or health care facility that provides intensive treatment medicine and constant monitoring for patients with severe and life-threatening illnesses or injuries.

words.tr: phrase. 产房；分娩室
words.ex: She was taken to the labour room when her contractions started.
words.ex_cn: 当她的宫缩开始时，她被送到了产房。
words.en: A room in a hospital where women give birth to babies.

words.tr: phrase. 产房；分娩室
words.ex: She was rushed to the delivery room when her contractions started.
words.ex_cn: 当她的宫缩开始时，她被迅速送到了产房。
words.en: A hospital room equipped for childbirth and immediate care of newborns.

words.tr: n. 停尸间；太平间
words.ex: The mortuary was filled with the bodies of the victims.
words.ex_cn: 停尸房里堆满了受害者的尸体。
words.en: A mortuary is a building or a room in a hospital where dead bodies are kept before they are buried or cremated.

words.tr: phrase. 手术室
words.ex: The surgeon walked into the operating room.
words.ex_cn: 外科医生走进了手术室。
words.en: A specialized room in a hospital where surgical operations are performed.

words.tr: n. 剧场；电影院；
words.ex: We watched a play at the theatre last night.
words.ex_cn: 我们昨晚在剧场看了一场戏。
words.en: A theatre is a building with a stage in it, on which plays, shows, and other performances take place.

words.tr: n. 药房；药剂学；
words.ex: He works at a small pharmacy near the park.
words.ex_cn: 他在公园附近的一家小药房工作。
words.en: A pharmacy is a shop or a department in a shop where medicines are prepared and sold.

words.tr: n. 化学家；药剂师；
words.ex: The chemist discovered a new element.
words.ex_cn: 这位化学家发现了一种新元素。
words.en: A chemist is a scientist who specializes in chemistry, or in some contexts, a person who is qualified to prepare and dispense drugs and medicines.

words.tr:
n. 病房；病室；选区；
v. 监护；守护；挡住；
words.ex: The patient is in ward 5.
words.ex_cn: 病人在5号病房。
words.en: A ward is a separate room in a hospital, typically one allocated to a particular type of patient, or a person, especially a child, who is under the protection or care of a legal guardian or a court.

words.tr: n. 皮炎
words.ex: He has dermatitis on his arms.
words.ex_cn: 他的胳膊上有皮炎。
words.en: Dermatitis is a condition in which the skin becomes red, swollen, and sore, sometimes with small blisters, resulting from direct irritation of the skin by an external agent or an allergic reaction to it.

words.tr: n. [眼科] 结膜炎
words.ex: He has conjunctivitis and his eyes are red.
words.ex_cn: 他得了结膜炎，眼睛发红。
words.en: Inflammation of the conjunctiva, the thin clear tissue that lies over the white part of the eye and lines the inside of the eyelid.

words.tr: n. 扁桃体炎
words.ex: He has tonsillitis and can't swallow food.
words.ex_cn: 他得了扁桃体炎，吞不下食物。
words.en: Tonsillitis is an infection or inflammation of the tonsils, which are the two lymph nodes located on each side of the back of your throat. It can cause a sore throat, fever, and difficulty swallowing.

words.tr: n. 脑膜炎
words.ex: Meningitis can be a life-threatening condition if not treated promptly.
words.ex_cn: 如果不及时治疗，脑膜炎可能会危及生命。
words.en: Meningitis is a serious illness in which there is inflammation of the meninges, the membranes covering the brain and spinal cord, usually caused by infection.

words.tr: phrase. 全身酸痛的；浑身疼痛的
words.ex: I have ache all over after playing soccer.
words.ex_cn: 踢完足球后我全身酸痛。
words.en: To feel pain throughout the entire body.

words.tr: phrase. 持续的疼痛；不间断的痛感
words.ex: She has been suffering from continuous pain in her back for months.
words.ex_cn: 她背部持续疼痛已经好几个月了。
words.en: Continuous pain refers to pain that persists over a long period without interruption.

words.tr: phrase. 持续性疼痛；长期疼痛；顽固疼痛
words.ex: He has persistent pain in his back.
words.ex_cn: 他背部有持续的疼痛。
words.en: Pain that continues for a long time and does not go away easily.

words.tr: phrase. 持续的疼痛；不间断的痛苦
words.ex: He feels constant pain in his back.
words.ex_cn: 他背部一直感到疼痛。
words.en: Continuous and unremitting physical suffering or discomfort.

words.tr: phrase. 疼痛时来时去；阵痛间歇出现
words.ex: Pain comes and goes when you run too much.
words.ex_cn: 跑太多时，疼痛会来来去去。
words.en: Describes pain that is intermittent or not constant.

words.tr: phrase. 轻微的疼痛
words.ex: He has a slight pain in his head.
words.ex_cn: 他头部有点轻微疼痛。
words.en: A slight pain is a minor or not very strong feeling of physical discomfort.

words.tr: phrase. 轻度疼痛；轻微痛感
words.ex: She felt a mild pain in her back after the long drive.
words.ex_cn: 长时间开车后，她感到背部有轻微的疼痛。
words.en: A slight or moderate discomfort or ache in a part of the body.

words.tr: phrase. 剧烈的疼痛；严重的痛楚
words.ex: He felt severe pain after the fall.
words.ex_cn: 他摔倒后感到剧烈疼痛。
words.en: Intense or extreme physical suffering or discomfort.

words.tr: phrase. 剧烈的疼痛；急性的疼痛
words.ex: He felt acute pain after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后感到剧烈的疼痛。
words.en: Acute pain is a type of pain that typically comes on suddenly and is often severe. It is usually a sign of tissue damage or injury and requires prompt medical attention.

words.tr: phrase. 剧烈疼痛；强烈的痛感
words.ex: He felt intense pain after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后感到剧烈的疼痛。
words.en: Intense pain refers to a very strong and severe feeling of physical discomfort or suffering.

words.tr: phrase. 钝痛的；隐痛的
words.ex: He felt a dull pain in his back after lifting the box.
words.ex_cn: 他搬完箱子后感到背部有一种钝痛。
words.en: A dull pain is a pain that is not sharp or intense, but rather a constant, mild ache or discomfort.

words.tr: phrase. 剧烈的疼痛；锐痛
words.ex: He felt a sharp pain in his leg.
words.ex_cn: 他感到腿里一阵剧痛。
words.en: A sharp pain is a sudden and intense feeling of discomfort or hurt.

words.tr: phrase. 刺骨般的剧痛；尖锐的刺痛
words.ex: The piercing pain in his chest made it difficult to breathe.
words.ex_cn: 他胸口的戳痛让他难以呼吸。
words.en: A sharp, intense pain that feels as if something sharp is piercing through the body.

words.tr: phrase. 刺痛；针刺般的疼痛
words.ex: She felt a prickling pain in her arm after the injection.
words.ex_cn: n. 注射后，她感到手臂有刺痛。
words.en: A sharp, stinging sensation often caused by minor irritation or nerve stimulation.

words.tr: phrase. 刺痛；麻刺感的疼痛
words.ex: His finger has a tingling pain after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他的手指在事故后有一种刺痛感。
words.en: A tingling pain is a sharp, pricking sensation that can occur in any part of the body, often due to nerve irritation or damage.

words.tr: phrase. 刺痛
words.ex: He felt a stabbing pain in his chest.
words.ex_cn: 他感到胸口一阵刺痛。
words.en: A sharp, sudden pain that feels like being stabbed.

words.tr: phrase. 发麻；针刺感；（因血液循环受阻而产生的）麻木刺痛感
words.ex: After sitting cross-legged for an hour, I had pins and needles in my foot.
words.ex_cn: 盘腿坐了一个小时后，我的脚感到发麻。
words.en: A tingling or prickling sensation in a part of the body, typically caused by temporary restriction of the blood supply.

words.tr: phrase. 剧烈的疼痛；酸痛的痛苦
words.ex: She felt a sore pain in her back after lifting the heavy box.
words.ex_cn: 她在搬重箱子后感到背部疼痛。
words.en: A sore pain is a feeling of discomfort or distress in a part of the body, often caused by injury or illness.

words.tr: n. 头痛；令人头痛的人（或事物）；
words.ex: He got a headache after working too long.
words.ex_cn: 他工作太长时间后得了头痛。
words.en: A headache is a pain in your head. If you say that something is a headache, you mean that it causes you difficulty or worry.

words.tr: adj. 头晕目眩的；头昏眼花的；
words.ex: He felt dizzy after spinning around quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他快速转圈后感到头晕目眩。
words.en: If you feel dizzy, you feel that you are losing your balance and are about to fall.

words.tr: adj. 使人晕眩的；头晕的；轻浮的
words.ex: She felt giddy after spinning around.
words.ex_cn: 她转圈后感到头晕目眩。
words.en: If you feel giddy, you feel unsteady and think that you are about to fall over, usually because you are not well or because you are excited or frightened.

words.tr: adj. 昏昏欲睡的；困倦的；催眠的
words.ex: He felt drowsy after lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他午饭后感到昏昏欲睡。
words.en: If you feel drowsy, you feel sleepy and cannot think clearly.

words.tr: n. 痰
words.ex: The doctor checked his sputum for bacteria.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了他的痰以寻找细菌。
words.en: Sputum is the mucus and other matter brought up from the lungs, bronchi, and trachea that one may cough up, often as a result of an infection or other condition.

words.tr: n. 痰；粘液
words.ex: He coughed up thick phlegm this morning.
words.ex_cn: 今天早上他咳出了浓痰。
words.en: Phlegm is a thick, sticky substance secreted by the mucous membranes of the respiratory passages, especially when one has a cold or other respiratory infection. It can also refer to one of the four humors in ancient and medieval physiology, believed to cause sluggishness or apathy.

words.tr: phrase. 呕吐；恶心；匆匆建造；产生；放弃
words.ex: He eats too fast and sometimes throws up.
words.ex_cn: 他吃得很快，有时会呕吐。
words.en: To vomit; to eject the contents of the stomach through the mouth.

words.tr: phrase. 喉咙发痒；嗓子痒
words.ex: I have an itchy throat and it's making me cough.
words.ex_cn: 我的喉咙痒，让我咳嗽。
words.en: An itchy throat is a sensation of irritation or tickling in the throat that often leads to coughing.

words.tr: v. 哮鸣; 喘息，发出呼哧呼哧的喘息声( wheeze的现在分词 )
words.ex: The old man was wheezing heavily after climbing the stairs.
words.ex_cn: 老人爬完楼梯后呼哧呼哧地喘着粗气。
words.en: Breathing with a whistling or rattling sound in the chest, as a result of obstruction in the air passages.

words.tr: v. 哆嗦；颤抖；
words.ex: He shivered in the cold wind.
words.ex_cn: 他在寒风中哆嗦。
words.en: If you shiver, your body shakes slightly because you are cold or frightened.

words.tr: n. 颤抖; v. 颤抖，哆嗦；敲碎，粉碎（shiver 的现在分词）
words.ex: The shivering child was wrapped in a warm blanket.
words.ex_cn: 颤抖的孩子被裹在温暖的毯子里。
words.en: If you are shivering, your body is shaking slightly because you are cold or frightened.

words.tr: phrase. 鼻塞；鼻腔充血
words.ex: He has nasal congestion because of a cold.
words.ex_cn: 他因为感冒而鼻塞。
words.en: Nasal congestion refers to the blockage of the nasal passages usually due to membranes lining the nose becoming swollen from inflamed blood vessels.

words.tr: phrase. 鼻塞；鼻子不通气
words.ex: He has a blocked nose from the cold.
words.ex_cn: 他因为感冒而鼻塞。
words.en: A condition where the nasal passages are obstructed, often due to inflammation or mucus.

words.tr:
adj. 发炎的；红肿的
v. 激怒；加剧；发炎；“inflame”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: His skin is inflamed after the bug bite.
words.ex_cn: 他被虫子叮咬后皮肤发炎了。
words.en: If part of your body is inflamed, it is red or swollen, usually as a result of an infection, injury, or illness.

words.tr:
adj. 肿胀的；上涨的
v. 膨胀；肿胀；“swell”的过去分词
words.ex: His ankle is swollen after the fall.
words.ex_cn: 他摔倒后脚踝肿了。
words.en: If a part of your body is swollen, it is larger and rounder than normal, usually as a result of injury or illness.

words.tr: phrase. 食欲不振；食欲减退；厌食
words.ex: He had a loss of appetite after the fever.
words.ex_cn: 发烧后他没了食欲。
words.en: A decrease in the desire to eat.

words.tr: phrase. 食欲不振；胃口差
words.ex: He has a poor appetite after the illness.
words.ex_cn: 他病后食欲不佳。
words.en: A lack of desire or enthusiasm for food, often indicating illness or lack of interest.

words.tr: n. 流感；流行性感冒；
words.ex: He caught influenza last winter.
words.ex_cn: 他去年冬天得了流感。
words.en: Influenza is an infectious disease caused by the influenza virus, characterized by fever, sore throat, muscle pain, severe headache, coughing, and weakness.

words.tr: n. 流感；流行性感冒；
words.ex: He stayed home because he had the flu.
words.ex_cn: 他因为得了流感待在家里。
words.en: The flu is an infectious disease characterized by fever, aches and pains, and respiratory symptoms.

words.tr: n. 超声波
words.ex: The doctor used ultrasound to check the baby.
words.ex_cn: 医生用超声波检查了婴儿。
words.en: Ultrasound is sound which is very high and cannot be heard by humans, used in medical examinations to produce images of the inside of the body.

words.tr: n. X射线
words.ex: The doctor used an x-ray to check his bone.
words.ex_cn: 医生用X光检查了他的骨头。
words.en: An X-ray is a type of radiation that can pass through most solid materials. X-rays are used in medicine to make images of the inside of the body.

words.tr: phrase. 磁共振成像（一种利用磁场和无线电波生成身体内部结构影像的医学成像技术）
words.ex: The doctor recommended magnetic resonance imaging to get a clearer picture of the injury.
words.ex_cn: 医生建议进行磁共振成像以更清楚地了解伤情。
words.en: A technique used in radiology to form pictures of the anatomy and the physiological processes of the body in both health and disease.

words.tr: abbr. 核磁共振成像
words.ex: The MRI scan revealed no abnormalities in the patient's brain.
words.ex_cn: 核磁共振成像显示患者的大脑没有异常。
words.en: Magnetic Resonance Imaging: a method used to create detailed images of the organs and tissues within the body using a magnetic field and radio waves.

words.tr: phrase. 计算机断层扫描（一种利用X射线生成身体内部详细图像的医学成像技术）
words.ex: The doctor recommended a 860.CT scan to get a detailed look at the internal injuries.
words.ex_cn: 医生建议进行860.CT扫描，以详细查看内部损伤。
words.en: A medical imaging technique using X-rays and computers to create detailed pictures of the inside of the body.

words.tr: phrase. 体格检查；身体检查；体检
words.ex: The doctor performed a thorough physical examination.
words.ex_cn: 医生进行了一次全面的身体检查。
words.en: A physical examination is a routine test your primary care provider (PCP) performs to check your overall health. A PCP may be a doctor, a nurse practitioner, or a physician assistant. The exam is also known as a wellness check. You don't have to be sick to request an exam.

words.tr: phrase. 体检
words.ex: You should have a health check every year.
words.ex_cn: 你应该每年做一次健康检查。
words.en: A health check is a medical examination to test your general state of health.

words.tr: 体检：一种通过医学检查来评估身体健康状况的过程。
words.ex: He had a medical checkup last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周做了体检。
words.en: A routine medical examination to assess a person's general health.

words.tr: phrase. 验血；血液试验
words.ex: The doctor ordered a blood test to check for any abnormalities.
words.ex_cn: 医生安排了血液检测，以检查是否有任何异常。
words.en: A blood test is a laboratory analysis performed on a blood sample that is usually extracted from a vein in the arm using a hypodermic needle, or via fingerprick. Blood tests are used to determine physiological and biochemical states, such as disease, mineral content, drug effectiveness, and organ function.

words.tr: phrase. 尿液检测；尿检
words.ex: The doctor ordered a urine test to check his health.
words.ex_cn: 医生要求做尿检以检查他的健康状况。
words.en: A test to analyze the urine for the presence of certain substances, such as glucose, protein, or bacteria, which can indicate various health conditions.

words.tr: phrase. 测量血压
words.ex: The nurse will measure blood pressure with a small machine.
words.ex_cn: 护士会用一个小机器测量血压。
words.en: To determine the force of blood against the walls of the arteries as the heart pumps it around the body.

words.tr: phrase. 测量身高和体重；量身高与体重
words.ex: The nurse will measure height and weight at the check-up.
words.ex_cn: 护士会在体检时测量身高和体重。
words.en: To determine the dimensions, quantity, or capacity of someone's height and weight.

words.tr: n. 标本；样品；
words.ex: The teacher showed a specimen of a butterfly.
words.ex_cn: 老师展示了一个蝴蝶标本。
words.en: A specimen is a single thing or example of something, especially one that is used to represent the whole group or type.

words.tr:
n. 样品；样本；
v. 抽样；
words.ex: The scientist tested the sample from the river.
words.ex_cn: 科学家测试了来自河流的样品。
words.en: A sample is a small quantity of a product, especially food, given to customers so that they can try it before buying it.

words.tr: n. 活组织检查；切片检查
words.ex: The doctor recommended a biopsy to determine the nature of the lump.
words.ex_cn: 医生建议进行活组织检查以确定肿块的性质。
words.en: A biopsy is a medical test involving the removal of cells or tissues for examination to determine the presence or extent of a disease.

words.tr: n. 结肠镜检查
words.ex: He had a colonoscopy to check his intestines.
words.ex_cn: 他做了结肠镜检查以检查肠道。
words.en: A medical examination in which a colonoscope is used to inspect the colon for abnormalities.

words.tr: n. 胃镜检查（法）
words.ex: He had a gastroscopy to check his stomach.
words.ex_cn: 他做了胃镜检查胃部。
words.en: A medical examination of the stomach using a gastroscope.

words.tr: n. 医学；药；
words.ex: He wants to study medicine at university.
words.ex_cn: 他想在大学学习医学。
words.en: Medicine is the science or practice of the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of disease.

words.tr: n. 药物; 敷药( medication的名词复数 ); 施药
words.ex: He takes medications every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上吃药。
words.en: Medications refer to substances used for medical treatment, especially pharmaceuticals.

words.tr: phrase. 处方药；须凭医生处方才能购买和使用的药物
words.ex: He takes prescription medicine for his pain.
words.ex_cn: 他服用处方药来缓解疼痛。
words.en: Medicine that can only be obtained with a prescription from a qualified medical practitioner.

words.tr: adj. 非处方的；（证券等）场外交易的
words.ex: He bought painkillers over-the-counter at the pharmacy.
words.ex_cn: 他在药店买了非处方止痛药。
words.en: Available for purchase without a prescription; traded directly between parties rather than on a formal exchange.

words.tr: phrase. 通用药物；非专利药；与品牌药具有相同活性成分的廉价替代药品
words.ex: Generic medicine is often more affordable than brand-name drugs.
words.ex_cn: 通用药物通常比品牌药物更便宜。
words.en: Generic medicine refers to a pharmaceutical drug that is equivalent to a brand-name product in dosage, strength, route of administration, quality, performance, and intended use, but is typically sold under its chemical name rather than a brand name.

words.tr: n. 抗菌素；抗生素；
words.ex: The doctor gave me an antibiotic for my infection.
words.ex_cn: 医生给我开了抗菌素治疗感染。
words.en: A substance that can kill or inhibit the growth of bacteria and other microorganisms.

words.tr: adj. 消炎的
words.ex: Ibuprofen is an anti-inflammatory drug that helps reduce pain and swelling.
words.ex_cn: 布洛芬是一种抗炎药，有助于减轻疼痛和肿胀。
words.en: An anti-inflammatory is a substance or treatment that reduces inflammation or swelling.

words.tr: n. 药膏；油膏；软膏
words.ex: He put ointment on his cut.
words.ex_cn: 他把药膏涂在伤口上。
words.en: A smooth substance that is rubbed on the skin to heal wounds or soothe pain.

words.tr: n. 麻醉；感觉缺失
words.ex: The patient felt no pain because of the anaesthesia.
words.ex_cn: 由于麻醉，病人没有感到疼痛。
words.en: Anaesthesia is the use of drugs to prevent pain during medical procedures.

words.tr: adj. 硬（脑）膜上的，硬脑膜外的 n. [医学] =epidural anesthesia
words.ex: She received an epidural before giving birth.
words.ex_cn: 她在分娩前接受了硬膜外麻醉。
words.en: An epidural is a type of anesthesia that is injected into the space around the spinal cord to block pain signals from the lower body during surgery or childbirth.

words.tr: phrase. 脊髓麻醉
words.ex: The patient opted for spinal anaesthesia during the surgery.
words.ex_cn: 患者在手术中选择了脊髓麻醉。
words.en: Spinal anaesthesia is a form of regional anaesthesia involving the injection of a local anaesthetic into the subarachnoid space, resulting in a loss of sensation in the lower part of the body.

words.tr: phrase. 全身麻醉；使病人失去知觉以进行手术的医疗方法
words.ex: The patient was under general anaesthesia during the surgery.
words.ex_cn: 手术期间病人处于全身麻醉状态。
words.en: General anaesthesia is a state of controlled unconsciousness during which a patient feels no pain and is unaware of the surgery being performed.

words.tr: phrase. 局部麻醉（使身体特定部位暂时失去痛觉，而患者保持清醒）
words.ex: The dentist used local anaesthesia before filling the cavity.
words.ex_cn: 牙医在补牙前使用了局部麻醉。
words.en: Local anaesthesia is a type of anaesthesia that numbs a specific part of the body, allowing for pain-free medical procedures without affecting consciousness.

words.tr:
n. 麻醉剂；麻醉药
adj. 麻醉的
words.ex: The doctor gave her an anaesthetic before the operation.
words.ex_cn: 医生在手术前给她打了麻醉剂。
words.en: A substance that causes insensitivity to pain, used especially in surgery.

words.tr: phrase. 止痛药
words.ex: He took a pain killer for his headache.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了一片止痛药来缓解头痛。
words.en: A pain killer is a drug that reduces or eliminates pain.

words.tr: n. 止痛药；镇痛剂；
words.ex: He took an analgesic for his headache.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了止痛药来缓解头痛。
words.en: An analgesic is a drug that is used to relieve pain.

words.tr: 短语动词. 打针，注射
words.ex: The nurse will give an injection to the patient.
words.ex_cn: 护士将给病人注射。
words.en: To administer a substance, typically a drug, into the body using a needle and syringe.

words.tr: 短语动词. 打针；注射
words.ex: The doctor advised him to have an injection to reduce the fever.
words.ex_cn: 医生建议他打一针来退烧。
words.en: To receive a dose of a drug or vaccine through a needle inserted into the skin.

words.tr:
n. 注射器；注水器；洗涤器
v. 注射；（用注水器）灌溉
words.ex: The nurse used a syringe to give him a shot.
words.ex_cn: 护士用注射器给他打了一针。
words.en: A syringe is a small tube with a thin hollow needle at the end. Syringes are used for putting liquids into things and for taking liquids out, for example for injecting drugs or for taking blood from someone's body.

words.tr: phrase. 【医学】给病人建立静脉输液；打点滴
words.ex: The nurse will put a drip in your arm to administer the medication.
words.ex_cn: 护士会在你的手臂上插入点滴以给药。
words.en: To insert a drip, typically for medical purposes such as administering fluids or medication intravenously.

words.tr: 短语动词. 接受静脉输液
words.ex: He has an IV drip because he is very sick.
words.ex_cn: 他因为病得很重，所以正在打点滴。
words.en: To receive fluids or medication directly into a vein through a tube.

words.tr:
n. 针脚；缝线；一针
v. 缝；缝合
words.ex: She sews a stitch to fix the tear.
words.ex_cn: 她缝一针来补破洞。
words.en: A stitch is a piece of thread that has been used to sew the edges of a wound together. It can also refer to a loop of thread or yarn resulting from a single pass or movement of the needle in sewing, knitting, or crocheting.

words.tr: n. 理疗；物理疗法
words.ex: He goes to physiotherapy after his surgery.
words.ex_cn: 他手术后去做物理治疗。
words.en: Physiotherapy is the treatment of disease, injury, or deformity by physical methods such as massage, heat treatment, and exercise rather than by drugs or surgery.

words.tr: n. 放射疗法
words.ex: She is undergoing radiotherapy for her cancer.
words.ex_cn: 她正在接受放射治疗以治疗癌症。
words.en: The treatment of disease, especially cancer, using X-rays or similar forms of radiation.

words.tr: n. 化疗；化学疗法；化学治疗
words.ex: He is receiving chemotherapy for cancer.
words.ex_cn: 他正在接受化疗治疗癌症。
words.en: The treatment of disease by the use of chemical substances, especially the treatment of cancer by cytotoxic and other drugs.

words.tr:
n. 绷带
v. 用绷带包扎
words.ex: He put a bandage on his cut finger.
words.ex_cn: 他在他割伤的手指上贴了绷带。
words.en: A bandage is a piece of material used to cover a wound or to support an injured part of the body.

words.tr: n. （邦迪牌）创可贴
words.ex: She put a Band-Aid on the cut.
words.ex_cn: 她在伤口上贴了一个创可贴。
words.en: A small adhesive bandage used to cover minor wounds or cuts. Also used metaphorically to describe a temporary solution to a problem.

words.tr: n. 外科手术
words.ex: He needs surgery for his broken arm.
words.ex_cn: 他需要做手术来治疗断掉的胳膊。
words.en: Surgery is the medical specialty that uses operative manual and instrumental techniques on a patient to investigate or treat a pathological condition such as a disease or injury, to help improve bodily function or appearance, or to repair unwanted ruptured areas.

words.tr: n. 运行；操作；手术；
words.ex: The operation of the machine is very smooth.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器的运行非常顺畅。
words.en: An operation is a planned activity involving many people performing various tasks.

words.tr: n. 步骤；程序；手续；
words.ex: Follow the procedure step by step.
words.ex_cn: 一步一步地按照步骤进行。
words.en: A procedure is a way of doing something, especially the usual or correct way.

words.tr: phrase. 侵入性操作；侵入性医疗程序（指需要刺破皮肤或进入体腔的诊断或治疗手段）
words.ex: The doctor recommended an invasive procedure to remove the tumor.
words.ex_cn: 医生建议进行侵入性手术以切除肿瘤。
words.en: A medical procedure that involves entering the body, usually by cutting or inserting instruments, to diagnose or treat a condition.

words.tr: phrase. 非侵入性操作；无创检查/治疗程序
words.ex: The doctor recommended a non-invasive procedure to diagnose the issue.
words.ex_cn: 医生推荐了一种非侵入性程序来诊断问题。
words.en: A non-invasive procedure is a medical procedure that does not require instruments to enter the body, minimizing the risk of complications and promoting faster recovery.

words.tr: phrase. 切除肿瘤
words.ex: The doctor will remove a tumour from the patient's lung.
words.ex_cn: 医生将从病人的肺部切除一个肿瘤。
words.en: To surgically excise or eliminate a tumour from the body.

words.tr: phrase. 移除肿块；去掉疙瘩
words.ex: The doctor decided to remove a lump from the patient's arm.
words.ex_cn: 医生决定移除病人手臂上的肿块。
words.en: To take away or eliminate a mass or swelling from a part of the body.

words.tr: phrase. 接受手术；动手术
words.ex: He will undergo surgery next week.
words.ex_cn: 他下周将接受手术。
words.en: To have a medical operation.

words.tr: phrase. 酒精成瘾；对酒精的依赖，指个体无法控制饮酒行为，导致身体和心理上的依赖
words.ex: The treatment program focuses on managing alcohol addiction.
words.ex_cn: 治疗方案的重点是管理酒癖。
words.en: Alcohol addiction refers to a physical and psychological dependence on alcohol, characterized by an inability to control or stop drinking despite negative consequences.

words.tr: phrase. 吸烟成瘾；对吸烟的依赖
words.ex: He struggled with smoking addiction for years before finally quitting.
words.ex_cn: 他多年来一直与吸烟成瘾作斗争，最终戒掉了。
words.en: Smoking addiction refers to the compulsive need to smoke tobacco, often leading to dependence and difficulty in quitting.

words.tr: phrase. 对某物上瘾的；沉溺于某事物的
words.ex: He is addicted to video games.
words.ex_cn: 他沉迷于电子游戏。
words.en: If someone is addicted to something, they like it very much and want to spend as much time as possible doing it or having it.

words.tr: phrase. 抵制吸烟的冲动；抗拒想抽烟的欲望
words.ex: She tried to resist smoking cravings by chewing gum.
words.ex_cn: 她试图通过嚼口香糖来抵抗吸烟的渴望。
words.en: To resist smoking cravings means to make an effort not to give in to the strong desire to smoke.

words.tr: phrase. 对香烟的强烈渴望；烟瘾
words.ex: He had a strong craving for cigarettes after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他在晚餐后对香烟有强烈的渴望。
words.en: A strong desire or urge for cigarettes.

words.tr: phrase. 渴望吸烟；对香烟有强烈渴望
words.ex: He craves for cigarettes when he is stressed.
words.ex_cn: 他一紧张就想抽烟。
words.en: To have a very strong desire for cigarettes.

words.tr: phrase. 疾病家族史；指家族中成员患有某种疾病的情况，常用于评估个体遗传或患病风险
words.ex: The doctor asked about my family history of disease to assess my risk factors.
words.ex_cn: 医生询问了我的家族病史以评估我的风险因素。
words.en: A record of the diseases and health conditions that have affected a person's family members, which can provide important information about the risk of developing certain diseases.

words.tr: phrase. 批量计费；集体计费（尤指医疗机构向政府或保险公司一次性提交多个患者的费用清单进行结算）
words.ex: The clinic offers bulk billing for all patients.
words.ex_cn: n. 该诊所对所有患者提供批量计费服务。
words.en: Bulk billing is a payment option in healthcare where the healthcare provider bills Medicare directly for the services provided to the patient, and the patient does not have to pay out of pocket.

words.tr: phrase. 由联邦医保支付的费用；医保覆盖费用
words.ex: Medicare cover fee is too high for old people.
words.ex_cn: 医疗保险的费用对老年人来说太高了。
words.en: Refers to whether a government health insurance program will pay for a medical cost.

words.tr: v. 报销；
words.ex: The company will reimburse you for your travel expenses.
words.ex_cn: 公司会报销你的旅行费用。
words.en: If you reimburse someone for something, you pay them back the money that they have spent or lost because of it.

words.tr: n. 偿还；偿付；退还
words.ex: He asked for reimbursement for his travel costs.
words.ex_cn: 他要求报销旅行费用。
words.en: The act of compensating someone for an expense or loss incurred.

words.tr: phrase. 将你转诊给专科医生；把你介绍给专家
words.ex: The doctor will refer you to a specialist.
words.ex_cn: 医生会把你转介给专家。
words.en: To direct a patient to a doctor with specialized knowledge.

words.tr: phrase. 常见的药物；普通药品
words.ex: Aspirin is a common medicine for headaches.
words.ex_cn: 阿司匹林是治疗头痛的常用药物。
words.en: Common medicine refers to medications that are widely used and readily available for treating common ailments.

words.tr: n. 必理痛（药品扑热息痛（acetaminophen）的一种品牌）
words.ex: He took a Panadol for his headache.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了一片扑热息痛来缓解头痛。
words.en: Panadol is a brand name for paracetamol (acetaminophen), used as a pain reliever and to reduce fever.

words.tr: n. 布洛芬（一种用于缓解疼痛、发烧和炎症的药物）
words.ex: I took some Nurofen to relieve my headache.
words.ex_cn: 我吃了一些布洛芬来缓解头痛。
words.en: Nurofen is a brand name for ibuprofen, used to relieve pain, fever, and inflammation.

words.tr: n. 阿司匹林（镇痛解热消炎药）
words.ex: He took aspirin for his headache.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了阿司匹林来缓解头痛。
words.en: Aspirin is a common drug that is used to reduce pain and inflammation.

words.tr: n. 青霉素
words.ex: The doctor gave him penicillin for his infection.
words.ex_cn: 医生给他开了青霉素治疗感染。
words.en: An antibiotic drug obtained from molds or produced synthetically, used to treat infections caused by bacteria.

words.tr: n. 醋氨酚
words.ex: Paracetamol is commonly used to relieve pain and reduce fever.
words.ex_cn: 醋氨酚常用于缓解疼痛和降低体温。
words.en: A drug used to reduce pain and fever. It is commonly used for the relief of headaches and other minor aches and pains and is a major ingredient in numerous cold and flu remedies.

words.tr: n. 抗生素
words.ex: The doctor gave me antibiotics for my infection.
words.ex_cn: 医生给我开了抗生素来治疗感染。
words.en: Antibiotics are medicines that are used to treat infections caused by bacteria.

words.tr: n. 反怀疑论者
words.ex: The anti-sceptic argued passionately against the doubters in the debate.
words.ex_cn: 反怀疑论者在辩论中热情地反驳怀疑者。
words.en: An anti-sceptic is a person who opposes or argues against scepticism, especially in philosophy or science.

words.tr: phrase. 抗过敏药物
words.ex: She took anti-allergic medicine to relieve her symptoms.
words.ex_cn: 她服用了抗过敏药物来缓解症状。
words.en: Medicine that prevents or relieves allergic reactions.

words.tr: n. 抗组织胺药
words.ex: He took an antihistamine for his runny nose.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了一片抗组胺药来缓解流鼻涕。
words.en: A substance that inhibits the physiological effects of histamine, used especially in the treatment of allergies.

words.tr:
adj. 通便的
n. 泻药；通便剂
words.ex: The doctor prescribed a laxative for his constipation.
words.ex_cn: 医生给他开了一种泻药来治疗便秘。
words.en: A laxative is a substance that you take to make you go to the toilet, especially when you are constipated.

words.tr: phrase. 用于治疗腹泻的药物；止泻药
words.ex: The doctor prescribed an anti-diarrheal medicine to help with my stomach issues.
words.ex_cn: 医生开了一种止泻药来帮助我解决胃部问题。
words.en: A medication used to prevent or treat diarrhea.

words.tr: n. 一种用于治疗腹泻的药物
words.ex: I took Imodium to relieve my diarrhea.
words.ex_cn: 我服用了Imodium来缓解我的腹泻。
words.en: Imodium is a medication used to treat diarrhea.

words.tr: n. 止痛药
words.ex: He took a painkiller for his headache.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了一片止痛药来缓解头痛。
words.en: A painkiller is a drug that reduces or removes physical pain.

words.tr: n. 一种用于预防和治疗晕动病的药物
words.ex: She took dramamine before the boat trip to avoid getting seasick.
words.ex_cn: 她在乘船旅行前服用了晕船药，以避免晕船。
words.en: A medication used to prevent and treat motion sickness.

words.tr: phrase. 尼古丁贴片（戒烟用的透皮贴片，通过皮肤缓慢释放尼古丁以缓解戒断症状）
words.ex: He used nicotine patches to help him quit smoking.
words.ex_cn: 他使用尼古丁贴片来帮助他戒烟。
words.en: Nicotine patches are small, adhesive patches that release nicotine into the bloodstream through the skin, used to help people quit smoking by reducing withdrawal symptoms.

words.tr: phrase. 安眠药
words.ex: He takes sleeping pills to help him sleep at night.
words.ex_cn: 他服用安眠药来帮助晚上入睡。
words.en: Sleeping pills are medicines that help people to sleep.

words.tr: phrase. 维生素药片；用于补充维生素的片剂
words.ex: She takes vitamin pills every morning to boost her immune system.
words.ex_cn: 她每天早上服用维生素片以增强免疫系统。
words.en: Vitamin pills are dietary supplements containing vitamins, which are essential nutrients that the body needs in small amounts to function properly.

words.tr: phrase. 铁剂片；补铁片
words.ex: She takes an iron tablet every morning to prevent anemia.
words.ex_cn: 她每天早上服用一片铁片剂以预防贫血。
words.en: A small, solid dose of iron, often in the form of a pill, used as a dietary supplement to prevent or treat iron deficiency.

words.tr: phrase. 服用药片以对抗腹泻
words.ex: You should take tablets against diarrhea if you feel unwell after eating.
words.ex_cn: 如果你在吃完东西后感到不适，应该服用药物以对抗腹泻。
words.en: To consume medication in order to counteract diarrhea.

words.tr: phrase. 康复中心；戒毒所；教养中心；复健机构
words.ex: He spent six months at a rehabilitation center after his surgery.
words.ex_cn: 他在手术后在一家康复中心度过了六个月。
words.en: A rehabilitation center is a facility where people go to recover from physical or mental illnesses, injuries, or addictions through various therapies and treatments.

words.tr:
n. 烟；烟雾；
v. 抽烟；冒烟；
words.ex: The fire produced thick smoke.
words.ex_cn: 火灾产生了浓烟。
words.en: Smoke consists of gas and small bits of solid material that are sent into the air when something burns.

words.tr: phrase. 重度吸烟者；烟瘾很大的人
words.ex: He is a heavy smoker and finds it hard to quit.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个烟瘾很大的人，发现很难戒烟。
words.en: A heavy smoker is someone who smokes a large amount of tobacco regularly.

words.tr: phrase. 一支接一支吸烟的人；连续吸烟者
words.ex: He is a chain smoker and finds it hard to quit.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个连续吸烟者，发现很难戒烟。
words.en: A chain smoker is a person who smokes cigarettes continuously, one after another.

words.tr: phrase. 暴饮；酗酒，指在短时间内大量饮酒的行为
words.ex: Binge drinking can lead to serious health problems.
words.ex_cn: n. 狂饮会导致严重的健康问题。
words.en: The consumption of an excessive amount of alcohol in a short period of time.

words.tr: phrase. 暴饮者； binge drinking 的人，指在短时间内大量饮酒的人
words.ex: He became a binge drinker after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后变成了一个酗酒者。
words.en: A binge drinker is someone who consumes a large amount of alcohol in a short period of time, often leading to intoxication.

words.tr: phrase. 戒烟；停止吸烟
words.ex: He quit smoking last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年戒烟了。
words.en: To stop the habit of smoking cigarettes or other tobacco products.

words.tr: 短语动词. 戒烟；停止吸烟
words.ex: He decided to give up smoking for the sake of his health.
words.ex_cn: 他决定为了健康戒烟。
words.en: To stop the habit of smoking cigarettes or other tobacco products.

words.tr: phrase. 戒酒；停止饮酒
words.ex: He decided to quit drinking soda.
words.ex_cn: 他决定戒掉喝苏打水。
words.en: To stop consuming alcohol, especially as a means of improving one's health or lifestyle.

words.tr: phrase. 戒酒；放弃饮酒
words.ex: He decided to give up drinking for his health.
words.ex_cn: 他决定为了健康戒酒。
words.en: To stop consuming alcoholic beverages, often for health or personal reasons.

words.tr: 短语. 除……之外（还）；对某物的增加
words.ex: Exercise is good for health in addition to making you feel happy.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼除了让你感到快乐外，还有益于健康。
words.en: Something that is added to something else to improve or complete it.

words.tr: phrase. 对某物的强烈渴望；对某事物的渴求
words.ex: He has a craving for chocolate every afternoon.
words.ex_cn: 他每天下午都特别想吃巧克力。
words.en: A strong desire for something.

words.tr: phrase. 服药；吃药
words.ex: He takes medicine every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上吃药。
words.en: To take medicine means to consume a substance, usually in the form of a pill or liquid, that is intended to treat or prevent disease or illness.

words.tr: phrase. 服用止痛药
words.ex: She decided to take painkillers to relieve her headache.
words.ex_cn: 她决定服用止痛药来缓解头痛。
words.en: To consume medication that relieves pain.

words.tr: phrase. 服用止痛药
words.ex: She had to take analgesics to relieve her headache.
words.ex_cn: 她不得不服用止痛药来缓解头痛。
words.en: To consume medications that relieve pain.

words.tr: phrase. 涂药；敷药；使用药物治疗
words.ex: The doctor will apply medicine to the wound to prevent infection.
words.ex_cn: 医生会在伤口上应用药物以防止感染。
words.en: To administer or use a substance, typically a drug, for therapeutic purposes.

words.tr: adj. 有效的；
words.ex: This medicine is effective against colds.
words.ex_cn: 这种药对感冒有效。
words.en: Something that is effective works well and produces the results that were intended.

words.tr: phrase. 药物有效的；疗效显著的
words.ex: This medicine effective against the flu.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物对流感有效。
words.en: A medicine effective is a drug or treatment that produces the desired therapeutic effect.

words.tr: phrase. 治疗工作；指与医疗、心理或社会服务相关的治疗性工作
words.ex: The treatment work on the water supply system was completed ahead of schedule.
words.ex_cn: 供水系统的处理工作提前完成了。
words.en: Treatment work refers to the processes and activities involved in managing, processing, or handling materials, substances, or systems to achieve a desired outcome, often in industrial, environmental, or medical contexts.

words.tr: n. 麻醉；感觉缺失
words.ex: The doctor gave him anesthesia before the surgery.
words.ex_cn: 医生在手术前给他打了麻醉。
words.en: Anesthesia is the use of drugs to prevent pain during surgery or other medical procedures.

words.tr: phrase. 全身麻醉；一种使患者在手术期间失去意识、无痛觉的状态
words.ex: He received general anesthesia before the surgery.
words.ex_cn: 他在手术前接受了全身麻醉。
words.en: A state of unconsciousness induced by medication, preventing pain during surgery.

words.tr: phrase. 局部麻醉；局部麻醉法
words.ex: The dentist used local anesthesia to numb the area before starting the procedure.
words.ex_cn: 牙医在开始手术前使用了局部麻醉来麻醉该区域。
words.en: A numbing of a specific area of the body using anesthetic agents, without affecting consciousness.

words.tr: n. 药物；药物治疗；药物处理；
words.ex: He took his medication every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上吃药。
words.en: Medication refers to a substance used for medical treatment, especially a medicine or drug.

words.tr: n. 药物；毒品；“drug”的复数；
words.ex: The doctor prescribed drugs for his headache.
words.ex_cn: 医生给他开了治疗头痛的药物。
words.en: A drug is a substance which is used to treat an illness, relieve a symptom, or modify a chemical process in the body for a specific purpose.

words.tr: n. 平板电脑；（刻有文字的）匾；
words.ex: He uses a tablet to read books.
words.ex_cn: 他用平板电脑读书。
words.en: A tablet is a small, flat computer that is controlled by touching the screen. It can also refer to a small, solid piece of medicine that you swallow.

words.tr: n. 药丸；药片；
words.ex: He took a pill for his headache.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了一粒药丸来缓解头痛。
words.en: A pill is a small solid mass of medicine that you swallow whole.

words.tr: n. 胶囊；
words.ex: He took a capsule for his headache.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了一粒胶囊来缓解头痛。
words.en: A capsule is a small container or case, especially one that is sealed and contains a dose of medicine, or a spacecraft's compartment for astronauts.

words.tr:
n. 液体；
adj. 液态的；
words.ex: Water is a common liquid.
words.ex_cn: 水是一种常见的液体。
words.en: A liquid is a substance which is not solid but which flows and can be poured, for example water.

words.tr: n. 糖浆；
words.ex: He poured syrup on his pancakes.
words.ex_cn: 他把糖浆倒在煎饼上。
words.en: A thick, sweet liquid made by dissolving sugar in boiling water, often used as a topping for desserts or as a sweetener in drinks.

words.tr: n. 奶油；护肤霜；
words.ex: She put cream on her coffee.
words.ex_cn: 她在咖啡里加了奶油。
words.en: Cream is the thick white or pale yellow fatty liquid which rises to the top when you boil milk, and which you can use in cooking or as a cosmetic.

words.tr: n. 乳液；
words.ex: She puts lotion on her hands after washing them.
words.ex_cn: 她洗手后在手上涂乳液。
words.en: A lotion is a liquid that you use to clean, improve, or protect your skin or hair.

words.tr: phrase. 草药；草本药物
words.ex: Herbal medicine has been used for centuries to treat a variety of ailments.
words.ex_cn: 草药医学被用于治疗各种疾病已有数百年历史。
words.en: Herbal medicine refers to the use of plants and plant extracts for therapeutic purposes. It is a form of alternative medicine that has been practiced for centuries across various cultures.

words.tr: phrase. 中药
words.ex: Traditional Chinese Medicine has been practiced for thousands of years.
words.ex_cn: 中医已经实践了数千年。
words.en: Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) is a broad range of medicine practices sharing common concepts which have been developed in China and are based on a tradition of more than 2,000 years, including various forms of herbal medicine, acupuncture, massage (Tui na), exercise (qigong), and dietary therapy.

words.tr: n. 胃；
words.ex: He ate too much and his stomach hurt.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多了，胃疼。
words.en: The stomach is the organ in your body where food is digested after you have eaten it.

words.tr: n. 肝脏
words.ex: He eats too much sugar and his liver is hurt.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多糖，他的肝脏受损了。
words.en: The liver is a large organ in the body that cleans the blood and produces bile, or a person who lives in a particular way.

words.tr: n. 肾，肾脏；肾，肾脏( kidney的名词复数 )；
words.ex: The doctor checked his kidneys for any damage.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了他的肾脏是否有损伤。
words.en: The kidneys are a pair of organs in the body that remove waste products from the blood and produce urine.

words.tr: n. 肺；“lung”的复数；
words.ex: Smoking damages your lungs.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟会损害你的肺。
words.en: The lungs are the organs in the chest that allow you to breathe.

words.tr: phrase. 胆囊（位于肝脏下方，用于储存和浓缩胆汁的器官）
words.ex: The gall bladder stores bile produced by the liver.
words.ex_cn: 胆囊储存肝脏产生的胆汁。
words.en: The gall bladder is a small organ that stores bile, a fluid produced by the liver to help digest fats. It is located beneath the liver.

words.tr: n. 心；心脏；
words.ex: He felt a pain in his heart.
words.ex_cn: 他感到心脏疼痛。
words.en: The heart is the organ in your chest that pumps the blood around your body. People also use heart to refer to the area of their chest that is closest to their heart.

words.tr: phrase. 膀胱；尿囊（储存尿液的器官）
words.ex: The urinary bladder stores urine until it is expelled from the body.
words.ex_cn: 膀胱储存尿液，直到它被排出体外。
words.en: The urinary bladder is a hollow organ in the body that stores urine until it is excreted.

words.tr: n. 附录；附件；
words.ex: The appendix contains extra data for the report.
words.ex_cn: 附录包含了报告的额外数据。
words.en: An appendix is a section at the end of a book that contains additional information. It can also refer to the small tube attached to the large intestine in the human body, known as the vermiform appendix.

words.tr: n. 神经；
words.ex: The nerve in his finger was damaged.
words.ex_cn: 他手指里的神经受到了损伤。
words.en: A nerve is a bundle of fibers that transmits impulses of sensation to the brain or spinal cord, and impulses from these to the muscles and organs. It also refers to the courage or control needed to do something difficult or dangerous.

words.tr: n. 船；容器；器皿；
words.ex: The fishing vessel sailed out at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 那艘渔船在黎明时出海。
words.en: A vessel is a large boat or a container for holding liquids.

words.tr: n. 动脉；干线；要道
words.ex: The artery carries blood from the heart.
words.ex_cn: 动脉将血液从心脏输送到身体。
words.en: An artery is a tube that carries blood from the heart to the rest of the body.

words.tr: n. 静脉；“vein”的复数；
words.ex: Blood flows through the veins back to the heart.
words.ex_cn: 血液通过静脉流回心脏。
words.en: Veins are the tubes in your body that carry blood back to your heart. They are part of the circulatory system, working alongside arteries to transport blood throughout the body.

words.tr:
n. 毛细血管
adj. 毛细管的；毛细作用的
words.ex: Blood moves through tiny capillary tubes.
words.ex_cn: 血液通过微小的毛细管流动。
words.en: A capillary is a very small blood vessel in the body that connects arteries and veins and allows the exchange of oxygen and nutrients between blood and tissues.

words.tr: n. 肠
words.ex: The intestine helps digest food.
words.ex_cn: 肠道帮助消化食物。
words.en: The part of the alimentary canal between the stomach and the anus.

words.tr: n. 脑；脑力；智力；
words.ex: The brain controls our thoughts and movements.
words.ex_cn: 大脑控制我们的思想和行动。
words.en: The brain is the organ inside your head that controls your body's activities and enables you to think and to feel things such as heat and pain.

words.tr: phrase. 传染病；由病原体引起并可在人与人之间传播的疾病
words.ex: Doctors work to stop infectious diseases.
words.ex_cn: 医生们努力阻止传染病。
words.en: Infectious diseases are disorders caused by organisms — such as bacteria, viruses, fungi or parasites. Many organisms live in and on our bodies. They're normally harmless or even helpful. But under certain conditions, some organisms may cause disease.

words.tr: phrase. 传染性疾病；具有传染性的疾病
words.ex: Hand washing can stop contagious diseases.
words.ex_cn: 勤洗手可以阻止传染病。
words.en: A contagious disease is a disease that spreads from one person or organism to another by direct or indirect contact.

words.tr: phrase. 传播流感
words.ex: He didn't cover his mouth when he sneezed, which helped spread the flu.
words.ex_cn: 他打喷嚏时没有捂住嘴，这有助于流感的传播。
words.en: To cause the flu virus to be passed from one person to another.

words.tr: 动词短语. 患上了流感
words.ex: He caught the flu and had to stay in bed for a week.
words.ex_cn: 他得了流感，不得不卧床休息一周。
words.en: To become infected with the influenza virus.

words.tr: phrase. 被……感染的；被……传染的；受……影响的
words.ex: He was infected with a rare virus.
words.ex_cn: 他被一种罕见的病毒感染了。
words.en: To be affected by a disease or a harmful influence.

words.tr: phrase. 传播疾病
words.ex: The rats spread disease in the old town.
words.ex_cn: 老鼠在老城里传播疾病。
words.en: To spread disease means to transmit or communicate a disease from one person or organism to another.

words.tr: phrase. 非处方药；可在药房直接购买的药品
words.ex: He bought over-the-counter medicine for his headache.
words.ex_cn: 他为头痛买了非处方药。
words.en: Medicine that can be bought without a prescription.

words.tr: phrase. 开处方药物；嘱咐用药
words.ex: The doctor prescribed medication for my headache.
words.ex_cn: 医生为我的头痛开了药。
words.en: To prescribe medication means to officially tell someone to take a particular medicine or treatment.

words.tr: phrase. 开药；处方用药
words.ex: The doctor prescribed medicines for my cold.
words.ex_cn: 医生为我的感冒开了药。
words.en: To prescribe medicines means to officially tell someone to take a particular medicine or treatment.

words.tr: phrase. 开处方；给予药物治疗指示
words.ex: The doctor will give prescription for medicine.
words.ex_cn: 医生会开药方。
words.en: To provide written instructions for medication from a doctor.

words.tr: 短语动词. 从药剂师那里购买
words.ex: He buys his medicine from pharmacist near home.
words.ex_cn: 他在家附近的药剂师那里买药。
words.en: To purchase something from a pharmacist, typically referring to buying medications or health-related products.

words.tr: phrase. 血压测试；测量血压的医疗检查
words.ex: The doctor recommended a blood pressure test to monitor my health.
words.ex_cn: 医生建议进行血压测试以监测我的健康状况。
words.en: A blood pressure test is a medical procedure used to measure the force of blood against the walls of the arteries as the heart pumps it around the body.

words.tr: phrase. 粪便检测；大便化验（用于诊断消化道疾病或感染）
words.ex: The doctor ordered a stool test to check for any infections.
words.ex_cn: 医生要求进行粪便检查以检查是否有感染。
words.en: A stool test is a medical examination of a sample of feces to diagnose or monitor diseases or conditions of the digestive system.

words.tr: n. [临床] 内窥镜检查；内视镜检查法；内视镜室
words.ex: The doctor used endoscopy to check his stomach.
words.ex_cn: 医生用内窥镜检查了他的胃。
words.en: A medical procedure that allows a doctor to look inside your body using an instrument called an endoscope.

words.tr: n. 心电图
words.ex: The doctor ordered an ECG to check the patient's heart rhythm.
words.ex_cn: 医生要求做心电图以检查患者的心律。
words.en: An ECG (electrocardiogram) is a test that records the electrical activity of the heart over a period of time using electrodes placed on the skin.

words.tr: phrase. 验光检查；视力测试
words.ex: I need to schedule an optometry test to check my vision.
words.ex_cn: 我需要预约一个验光测试来检查我的视力。
words.en: A test conducted by an optometrist to assess the health of the eyes and determine the need for corrective lenses.

words.tr: phrase. 进行检查；执行检查
words.ex: The mechanic will perform a check on the car's engine.
words.ex_cn: v. 机械师将对汽车的发动机进行检查。
words.en: To carry out an examination or inspection to ensure that something is in proper condition or functioning correctly.

words.tr: phrase. 进行核查；做检查；核对
words.ex: The technician will run a check on the system to ensure everything is working properly.
words.ex_cn: v. 技术人员将对系统进行检查，以确保一切正常运行。
words.en: To perform a verification or inspection to ensure accuracy, functionality, or security.

words.tr: phrase. 进行某些测试；做一些检测
words.ex: The engineer needs to run some tests on the new software.
words.ex_cn: 工程师需要对这款新软件进行一些测试。
words.en: To perform a series of checks or experiments to assess functionality, quality, or performance.

words.tr: phrase. 进行其他任何测试
words.ex: We need to do any other tests to confirm the results.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要进行其他测试以确认结果。
words.en: To perform additional tests or examinations.

words.tr: 短语. 得到我的结果；获取我的成绩或测试结果
words.ex: I need to get my results before the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 我需要在会议前获取我的结果。
words.en: To obtain or receive the outcomes or findings of something.

words.tr: phrase. 公布结果；发布成绩；结果出炉
words.ex: The results out last week were surprising.
words.ex_cn: 上周公布的结果令人惊讶。
words.en: to produce or achieve something, especially after effort or testing

words.tr: phrase. + adv. 还没回来吗？（用于询问某人是否已经返回）
words.ex: He has not come back yet.
words.ex_cn: 他还没有回来。
words.en: still not yet; used to indicate that something has not happened or been completed

words.tr: phrase. 被诊断患有（某种疾病）
words.ex: He was diagnosed with diabetes last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年被诊断出患有糖尿病。
words.en: To identify a disease or condition in someone through medical examination.

words.tr: n. 治疗；处理；待遇；
words.ex: The doctor gave him proper treatment for the infection.
words.ex_cn: 医生给他提供了针对感染的适当治疗。
words.en: The act or manner of treating someone or something, especially in a medical context.

words.tr: phrase. 在接受治疗；处于治疗中
words.ex: She is currently on treatment for her chronic illness.
words.ex_cn: 她目前正在接受慢性病的治疗。
words.en: The phrase 'on treatment' refers to the state of undergoing medical treatment or therapy for a condition or illness.

words.tr: phrase. 接受治疗；接受处理
words.ex: She is receiving treatment for her illness.
words.ex_cn: 她正在接受疾病治疗。
words.en: The act of undergoing medical care or therapy for a health condition.

words.tr: phrase. 接受治疗；进行医疗处理
words.ex: He had to undergo treatment for his illness.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不接受治疗以应对他的疾病。
words.en: To undergo treatment means to receive medical care or therapy for a health condition.

words.tr: phrase. 接受治疗；接受处理
words.ex: He receives treatment for his back pain.
words.ex_cn: 他正在接受背痛的治疗。
words.en: To undergo medical care or therapy for an illness or injury.

words.tr: 被对待；被处理；被治疗
words.ex: She should be treated with respect.
words.ex_cn: 她应该受到尊重。
words.en: To be treated means to be dealt with or handled in a particular way, often with care or respect.

words.tr: 短语，表示‘病情可以被治疗’或‘状况能够得到处理’
words.ex: The condition can be treated with medicine.
words.ex_cn: 这种状况可以通过药物治疗。
words.en: to be dealt with or managed medically

words.tr: condition: n. 状况；病情；条件；be cured: 被治愈
words.ex: His condition be cured after the medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他的病情在服药后被治愈了。
words.en: to be completely healed or made healthy again

words.tr: phrase. 不可治疗的；无法医治的；不能处理的
words.ex: The disease is not treatable with current medical technology.
words.ex_cn: 这种疾病无法用当前的医疗技术治疗。
words.en: Not able to be treated or cured with medical intervention.

words.tr: adj. 能治疗的；能处理的
words.ex: This disease is treatable with medicine.
words.ex_cn: 这种病可以通过药物治疗。
words.en: If a disease or condition is treatable, it can be cured or made better with medical care.

words.tr:
adj. 不能治愈的；无可救药的
n. 患不治之症者；不能治愈的人
words.ex: The disease is incurable.
words.ex_cn: 这种病无法治愈。
words.en: If someone has an incurable disease, they cannot be cured of it.

words.tr: adj. 可医治的；可治愈的
words.ex: This disease is curable with medicine.
words.ex_cn: 这种病可以通过药物治愈。
words.en: A curable disease or medical condition is one that can be cured.

words.tr: phrase. 正在服药；正在接受药物治疗
words.ex: She has been on medication for her chronic condition.
words.ex_cn: 她一直在为她的慢性病服药。
words.en: Taking prescribed drugs for medical treatment.

words.tr: v. 注入；
words.ex: The nurse will inject medicine into his arm.
words.ex_cn: 护士将把药水注入他的手臂。
words.en: To inject a substance such as a medicine or drug means to put it into someone's body using a needle and a syringe.

words.tr: n. 注入；
words.ex: The doctor gave him an injection for the pain.
words.ex_cn: 医生给他打了一针来缓解疼痛。
words.en: An injection is the act of putting a liquid, especially a drug, into a person's body using a needle and a syringe.

words.tr: v. 射击；拍摄（电影）；疾驰；“shoot”的过去式和过去分词； n. 照片；射击；射门；
words.ex: He shot the target with his gun.
words.ex_cn: 他用枪射击了目标。
words.en: A shot is an act of shooting a gun, or the sound that this makes. It can also refer to an attempt to do something, a photograph, or an injection.

words.tr: phrase. 胰岛素注射（指将胰岛素通过皮下注射方式给药以控制血糖水平）
words.ex: He needs to take insulin injections every day to manage his diabetes.
words.ex_cn: 他需要每天注射胰岛素来控制他的糖尿病。
words.en: Insulin injections are a medical treatment used to manage blood sugar levels in people with diabetes by administering insulin directly into the body.

words.tr: phrase. 接受疫苗接种；接种疫苗
words.ex: All children should receive vaccination before starting school.
words.ex_cn: 所有儿童在上学前都应接种疫苗。
words.en: To receive vaccination means to be given a vaccine to protect against a particular disease.

words.tr: n. 免疫；免疫作用
words.ex: The child received immunization against measles.
words.ex_cn: 孩子接种了麻疹疫苗。
words.en: The process by which an individual's immune system becomes fortified against an agent (known as the immunogen).

words.tr: phrase. 已接种疫苗的；接受了疫苗注射的
words.ex: It is important to be vaccinated against the flu every year.
words.ex_cn: 每年接种流感疫苗是很重要的。
words.en: To receive a vaccine in order to protect against a particular disease.

words.tr: phrase. 被免疫的；获得免疫力的
words.ex: Children should be immunized against measles.
words.ex_cn: v. 儿童应该接种麻疹疫苗。
words.en: To be immunized means to be made immune or resistant to an infectious disease, typically by the administration of a vaccine.

words.tr: n. 治疗；疗法；
words.ex: He is receiving therapy for his back pain.
words.ex_cn: 他正在接受治疗以缓解背痛。
words.en: Therapy is the treatment of someone with mental or physical illness without the use of drugs or operations.

words.tr: n. 放射学；辐射学
words.ex: He works in the radiology department at the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 他在医院的放射科工作。
words.en: Radiology is the branch of medicine that uses medical imaging to diagnose and treat diseases within the body.

words.tr: n. 水疗法
words.ex: She underwent hydrotherapy to ease her back pain.
words.ex_cn: 她接受了水疗以缓解背痛。
words.en: Hydrotherapy is the use of water in the treatment of disease or injury.

words.tr: phrase. 动手术
words.ex: He will have an operation next week.
words.ex_cn: 他下周要做手术。
words.en: Undergo a medical procedure performed by a surgeon.

words.tr: phrase. 接受手术；动手术
words.ex: He had to undergo an operation to remove the tumor.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不接受手术以切除肿瘤。
words.en: To undergo an operation means to have a surgical procedure performed on one's body, typically to treat a medical condition or injury.

words.tr: v. 恢复；重新获得；复原；
words.ex: He will recover from the illness soon.
words.ex_cn: 他很快就会从疾病中恢复。
words.en: If you recover from an illness or an injury, you become well again. If you recover something that has been lost or stolen, you find it or get it back.

words.tr: n. 恢复；复苏；
words.ex: He needs time for recovery after the surgery.
words.ex_cn: 他手术后需要时间恢复。
words.en: The process of becoming well again after an illness or injury, or the process of returning to a normal condition after a period of difficulty.

words.tr: phrase. 完全康复的；彻底恢复的
words.ex: He is fully recovered from the flu.
words.ex_cn: 他已完全从流感中康复。
words.en: completely healed or restored to health

words.tr: v. 送…住院；送…住院，使留医( hospitalize的过去式和过去分词 )；
words.ex: He was hospitalized after the car accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在车祸后被送入医院。
words.en: If someone is hospitalized, they are sent or admitted to a hospital.

words.tr: phrase. 被送入医院接受治疗
words.ex: He was admitted to hospital after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后被送进医院。
words.en: If someone is admitted to hospital, they are taken into hospital for treatment and kept there until they are well enough to go home.

words.tr: phrase. 已出院的；指病人经治疗后被医院允许离开
words.ex: She was discharged from hospital after a week of treatment.
words.ex_cn: 她在接受了一周的治疗后出院了。
words.en: To be allowed to leave the hospital after receiving medical treatment.

words.tr: phrase. 住院手续；入院程序
words.ex: The hospital has streamlined its hospitalization procedures to reduce waiting times.
words.ex_cn: 医院已经简化了其住院程序以减少等待时间。
words.en: The process or set of actions required for admitting a patient into a hospital for treatment.

words.tr: phrase. 完成文书工作；办理书面手续
words.ex: He needs to complete paperwork for the new job.
words.ex_cn: 他需要为新工作完成文书工作。
words.en: To finish all the necessary documents or forms.

words.tr: 从未住院过的；从未接受过住院治疗的
words.ex: She has never been hospitalized in her life.
words.ex_cn: phrase. 她一生中从未住过院。
words.en: phrase. Not having been admitted to a hospital for medical treatment.

words.tr: phrase. 首次住院的；第一次因病住进医院的
words.ex: This is her first time hospitalized since the accident.
words.ex_cn: 这是她自事故以来的首次住院。
words.en: The initial instance of being admitted to a hospital for medical treatment.

words.tr: 短语动词. 受伤；受到伤害
words.ex: He gets injured when he falls off the bike.
words.ex_cn: 他从自行车上摔下来受伤了。
words.en: To suffer physical harm or damage to the body.

words.tr: adj. 受伤的；负伤的； v. “wound”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The wounded soldier was taken to the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 受伤的士兵被送往医院。
words.en: If someone is wounded, they are injured by something that damages their body, especially in a battle.

words.tr:
adj. 扭伤的
v. 扭伤；“sprain”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He sprained his ankle while running.
words.ex_cn: 他跑步时扭伤了脚踝。
words.en: If you sprain a joint such as your ankle or wrist, you accidentally twist it in a violent way, causing it to swell and become painful.

words.tr: v. 擦伤；挫伤；出现伤痕；
